title: HLC clock mutex held across IPFS write and SQLite insert — POSTs serialize
description: lifecycle.rs run_post_pipeline: 'let mut clock = stores.clock.lock().await; append_to_groups(..., &mut clock, ...).await; drop(clock)'. The Mutex is held across the full append_to_groups await, which includes IPFS write latency and SQLite inserts. Any concurrent POST waits on this mutex. Expected impact: under load (multiple simultaneous POST clients), effective POST throughput is serialized to a single pipeline per server. This is intentional for HLC correctness (timestamps must be monotone), but the clock only needs to be held while generating the timestamp — not for the entire storage write. Fix: advance clock to get timestamp, drop lock, then pass timestamp into a refactored append_to_groups that doesn't need the clock handle.
